questions.prompt: An incoming event is delivered twice after a webhook retry. What should prevent a duplicate record?

options.a: Use a persistent event identifier and check whether the event was processed already
options.b: Append every event even when identifiers match exactly
options.c: Generate a new identifier on each retry to hide duplicates

questions.feedback: A stable idempotency key prevents one business event from triggering repeated effects.

questions.prompt: A weekly report trigger runs again because a connector timed out after writing data. Which strategy is safest?

options.a: Email the identical report to every client twice
options.b: Ignore the possibility that connectors retry
options.c: Check the stored report/run identifier and avoid repeated external effects

questions.feedback: A stable idempotency key prevents one business event from triggering repeated effects.

questions.prompt: A summary workflow requests the ability to delete every company document. What is appropriate?

options.a: Grant administrator rights to prevent future permission errors
options.b: Place master tokens inside a public workflow prompt
options.c: Restrict access to the necessary fields and prohibit unrelated deletion rights

questions.feedback: Least-privilege access and credential separation should be part of workflow design.

questions.prompt: A no-code automation reads order statuses to prepare a weekly count. What should its scope include?

options.b: Read-only access to approved order columns and the reporting date range
options.c: Rights to export all employee records and customer correspondence

questions.feedback: Least-privilege access and credential separation should be part of workflow design.

questions.prompt: An AI-generated invoice assistant encounters a changed bank beneficiary. How should the flow proceed?

options.a: Overwrite the original beneficiary without a review record
options.b: Stop any payment and require independent human verification of the bank details
options.c: Approve payment automatically because it was well phrased

questions.feedback: Irreversible or external actions require checks and explicit accountable human approval.

questions.prompt: An automatic social scheduler drafts a claim about an unconfirmed product discount. What should happen before posting?

options.a: Require an authorized editor to check pricing facts and approve the exact version before scheduling
options.b: Send the post first and ask the editor to review later
options.c: Have the model invent a plausible discount to complete the schedule

questions.feedback: Irreversible or external actions require checks and explicit accountable human approval.

questions.prompt: A manual weekly report took 90 minutes; the new flow takes 35 plus 20 minutes for review. What net time saving can be claimed?

options.a: 35 minutes saved per comparable run, subject to real measurement
options.b: 90 minutes saved because the AI step is immediate
options.c: 55 minutes saved while ignoring human review time

questions.feedback: Measure total supervised work and validate normal and exceptional paths before declaring a workflow ready.

questions.prompt: An automation passes a standard sample but fails when a required field is absent. What next step supports release readiness?

options.a: Claim the system is production-ready because one normal example passed
options.b: Hide the failed run and discard its test evidence
options.c: Record the missing-field failure, add safe exception handling and retest before activation

questions.feedback: Measure total supervised work and validate normal and exceptional paths before declaring a workflow ready.
